findings.title: Reread threshold is presented as proof of context eviction
findings.what: The tile derives affected sessions solely from parseFileReread and its three-read threshold, then describes every qualifying case as “eviction-driven context thrash.” Three reads establish repetition, not why the reads occurred; tight-loop intentional reads and reads without any compaction receive the same causal label and estimated-waste framing.
findings.fix: Rename the metric and caption to a non-causal repeated-read heuristic and state the threshold/estimate caveat, or require an explicit eviction/compaction provenance signal before applying the eviction-driven label.
findings.acceptance: Render the tile with one session containing three closely spaced reads of the same file and no compaction evidence. It may report a repeated-read candidate and estimated tokens, but must not call it eviction-driven context thrash; add a separate fixture with qualifying provenance if that stronger label remains supported.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the cited component lines at baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. The fraction denominator is toolData.length and the numerator comes directly from the reread summary; no eviction, time-spread, or compaction condition is applied. Comparison-only inspection of the baseline parser confirmed qualification is readCount >= threshold, while the batch test fixture demonstrates that three reads one minute apart are sufficient to qualify.
